einzeiler: Thomas Massie discusses the Epstein files, government overreach, and congressional…
kurzfassung: Congressman Thomas Massie joins the show to discuss the behind-the-scenes battle over releasing the Epstein files and why the executive branch is withholding millions of documents. He details the strategy behind the initial transparency act and outlines a new legislative push to grant legal standing to survivors and state attorneys general. The conversation also covers foreign policy failures, constitutional war powers, and the political landscape following his primary defeat.
stichpunkte: Thomas Massie details the passage and impact of the first Epstein Files Transparency Act, which forced the release of three million documents.
The Justice Department is accused of unlawfully withholding millions of additional documents and utilizing the deliberative process privilege to block accountability.
Massie explains the introduction of the Epstein Files Transparency Act Part Two, designed to grant legal standing to survivors, state attorneys general, and members of Congress.
The new legislation specifically targets crimes and evidence tied to Zorro Ranch in New Mexico to enable state-level prosecutions.
Discussion covers the failure of the executive branch and intelligence agencies to adhere to war powers legislation regarding ongoing conflicts in the Middle East.
Massie reflects on his primary election loss, noting the heavy financial influence of outside lobbies and the generational divide in voter support.
The hosts and Massie examine high-level connections involving Jeffrey Epstein and intelligence apparatuses, including the CIA and Mossad.

clips.hook: Drafting legislation entirely outside the usual channels
clips.text: A major transparency bill was successfully written from scratch within twenty-four hours without any involvement from lobbyists or career congressional staffers.
When questioned about the timeline for releasing remaining documents, the attorney general abruptly dismissed them as illicit pornography that nobody would want to see.

clips.hook: Bypassing federal stonewalling through state prosecution
clips.text: The proposed second transparency bill provides state authorities with direct access to records and legal avenues to pursue unresolved crimes independently of federal agencies.
